claims: The Balkans is a region in Southeast Europe.
The Balkans is bordered by the Adriatic Sea, the Ionian Sea, and the Black Sea.
The core countries of the Balkans include Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania, Serbia, and portions of Kosovo, Slovenia, and Turkey.
The name Balkans is derived from the Turkish word for the Balkan Mountains.
The Balkan Mountains run through Bulgaria.
The Balkans is home to a mix of Christianity (Orthodox and Catholic) and Islam.
The Balkans has a long history of Judaism.
Dominant languages in the Balkans include Serbian, Croatian, Bulgarian, Macedonian, Romanian, Albanian, Greek, and Turkish.
Dubrovnik, Croatia is a walled city.
Ohrid is a historic town in North Macedonia.
The Balkans includes the Dinaric Alps.
The Balkans includes the Rhodope Mountains.
The Balkans was historically influenced by the Romans.
The Balkans was historically influenced by the Byzantines.
The Balkans was historically influenced by the Ottoman Empire.
Plitvice Lakes National Park is in Croatia.
Belgrade is the cultural center of Serbia.
The Balkans had conflict in the 1990s.
